Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
250 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat building this week with temperatures in the upper
  90s/100s and heat indices of 104-112F. Heat Advisories likely at
  times during the upcoming work week.

- Patchy fog possible during the early to mid-morning hours for at
  least the next few days.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1253 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

A strong ridge of high pressure building over the Southern Plains
will bring hot conditions all week long with dangerous heat
possible during the afternoon hours. A combination of this high
pressure, abnormally warm temperatures aloft, and daytime heating
will give way to afternoon high temperatures near 100 degrees all
week long for non-coastal areas. Temperatures may peak around 
96-99 on Monday, but triple digit highs may begin to appear around
highly urbanized areas by Tuesday with most inland locations
reaching 100-103 degrees by Thursday. Add in the humidity and we
will be seeing heat indicies around 105-108 degrees on Monday and
then 106-110 (or higher) Tuesday through the end of the week.
Urbanized areas (especially the Houston Metro) may see heat 
indices higher than 108 degrees on Monday for a couple hours
during the afternoon. A Heat Advisory may be issued during later 
shifts for Monday if these higher heat indices are expected to be
more widespread or hotter. The likelihood of a Heat Advisory
become much higher by Tuesday as the dangerous heat become more
widespread.

Rain chance remain near zero for much of this week thanks to
increased subsidence from the dominating high pressure overhead.
This high pressure is forecasted to slide westward by this weekend
allowing for some shortwaves to slide down into East Texas along
the eastern edge of the ridge. This would bring a return of rain
chances by as early as Saturday afternoon and continue into the
start of the following week. But, this is highly dependent on how
far west the high pressure slides. If it stays further east, or is
stronger, then the rain chances would also stay to our east. 

Fowler

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 545 AM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

A fcst of persistence for the most part. Like the past couple
days, we're seeing some intermittent, patchy MVFR vsby/cigs 
across parts of the area...mainly outside the metro terminals. 
These should lift by mid morning with VFR conditions generally 
prevailing for the remainder of the day until we do it all over 
again later tonight. We might see a few light shra dotting some 
of the coastal counties this morning. Some of the hires guidance 
has shown some consistency showing an isolated cell or two 
developing in the IAH/CXO areas between 22-01z, so threw in a 
PROB30 there. 47

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1253 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Light to occasionally moderate southerly/southwesterly winds and 
2-4 ft seas will prevail for most of this week. No significant
weather concerns expected.

Fowler

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
621 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat this week with temperatures in the upper 90s to
  100s and heat indices of 106-110F. Heat Advisories are likely 
  at times next week.

- Later in the week, upper ridging begins to lose its control
  overhead, allowing temps to moderate slightly and rain chances 
  to return to the forecast
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Saturday)
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Hot weather will continue to be the main concern across the 
region. Aloft, ridging is centered over the Four Corners region 
and extends to the Gulf Coast. This is a fairly strong ridge for 
this July, with 500 mb heights over the CWA above the 
climatological 90th percentile. Persistent sinking air associated 
with this ridge will keep our skies clear and rain chances below 
10%. At the surface, high pressure is located in the eastern Gulf,
creating continuous but weak onshore flow. Dew points will slowly
increase, then plateau into the mid-70s inland and the upper 70s 
along the coast. With the clear skies daytime heating will help 
mix down some of the dry air limiting dew points. Temperatures 
will also steadily increase, with highs in the upper 90s and close
to triple digits for northern parts of the CWA. Heat index values
will approach the +108 criteria for a Heat Advisory each day 
during the work week, with the hottest days of the week looking 
like Tuesday and Wednesday. Even without heat advisories, make 
sure to stay hydrated and take plenty of breaks from the heat.

This pattern will remain stagnant for the next several days with
little change to our synoptic setup. We will start to see the
ridge begin to weaken and rebuild in the desert southwest. This
will allow for troughs to rotate around the ridge increasing our
rain chances for the end of the week. With the increase in rains
temperatures will decrease slightly back down into the mid 90s.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 619 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

A few clouds near 5000ft will continue to stream across the region
as we head towards sunset, giving way to mostly clear skies
overnight. Light to moderate SW winds will become light to near
calm overnight, which may allow for some patchy fog to develop at
AEX. Otherwise, VFR conditions prevail. 


&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Light onshore winds and calm seas will continue for the next five
days. Rain chances will return on Thursday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1217 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Hot and dry weather will continue well into the work week. Rain
chances will be near zero until Thursday. MinRH will be between 40
and 60 percent through next Friday with RH recovery around 90%.
